question: Why did several early Queen albums carry a sleeve note saying no synthesisers were used?
answer: Because listeners assumed the layered sounds were synthesised. Brian May built orchestral sections by recording his home-made guitar in many harmonised parts, one line at a time; the choirs were three band members overdubbed again and again. Their first album with a synthesiser was The Game, in 1980. The orchestra was one guitar, stacked.
move: When a result looks machine-made, ask how many patient passes built it.
source: Queen, A Night at the Opera, 1975
reference: Queen, A Night at the Opera, EMI, 1975, sleeve notes
